subject: Next steps: Scaling deep-dive & sizing call for Acme Edge

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Next steps: Scaling deep-dive & sizing call for Acme Edge

Hi Sam — great conversation earlier today, thanks for walking through the integration goals and the expected query patterns. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock a dedicated capacity sizing session (technical deep-dive + throughput validation):

Recap (1 line): you need a low-latency generator for real-time personalization with high peak concurrency during batch windows.

Proposed next step: a 60–90 minute sizing call where we pair your infra/engineers with our performance team to: 
- validate peak throughput requirements,
- align on p95/p99 latency targets,
- review load profile and tokenization assumptions,
- agree on a mutual action plan and timeline.

Suggested slots (all PST):
- Wed Nov 25, 2026 — 14:00–15:30 PST
- Thu Nov 26, 2026 — 10:00–11:30 PST

Who to include from your side: engineering lead, SRE/infra, a product owner who can speak to query shapes. From our side: Marissa (AE), Soojin (Solutions Eng) and I; we'll bring a perf engineer for live throughput checks.

I've attached a short mutual action plan and the load-profile CSV you can use to populate a pre-call sample. If you can confirm the preferred slot and attach a simple traffic matrix (peak qps, average qps, token counts per request), we'll send a calendar invite and pre-call checklist.

Attachments: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_ACMEEDGE.xlsx, acme_edge_load_profile.csv

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma

Thanks Nikhil — that works, really appreciate the clear agenda. We prefer Thu Nov 26 at 10:00 PST if that slot is still open.

A couple quick clarifications before we lock:
- Peak target: ~500 concurrent inference threads during nightly batch windows (burst to ~1,200 qps for short spikes).
- Latency goal: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms for generation workloads (typical generation length ~512 tokens).
- Data residency: must stay in US regions — can you confirm region options for Dedicated?

I'll loop in our infra lead (Priya) and procurement (contracts@acmeedge.com) so they have visibility — procurement will likely want the mutual action plan and a preliminary SOW for budget planning.

Hi Sam — thanks, Thu Nov 26 10:00 PST works for our team. Quick technical note and a short pre-call checklist so the session is productive:

Short answers to your bullets:
- Dedicated region options: we can provision Dedicated capacity in us-west-2 or us-east-1; we'll confirm exact node placement during procurement but both satisfy US residency.
- 1,200 qps spikes are feasible with a properly sized pool — we'll validate during the call. p95/p99 targets depend on model choice, sequence length, and batch sizing; we'll run live microbenchmarks and share expected unit economics.

Pre-call checklist (please attach when you reply):
1) A short CSV with expected QPS by hour (you can use the attached acme_edge_load_profile.csv as a template).
2) A sample request (JSON) including tokenized lengths or an example prompt so we can estimate tokenization overhead.
3) Any compliance constraints (retention windows, logging/PII rules) we should know before the run.

Agenda (60–90m):
- 10m: introductions & goals
- 20m: architecture & traffic walkthrough (Acme infra)
- 25m: perf baseline & throughput testing (we run microbenchmarks)
- 15m: rollout/ops plan and SLA/region discussion
- 10m: procurement/next actions (MUTUAL ACTION PLAN review)

I'll bring a perf engineer and an ops lead. We'll also prepare a short checklist of configuration knobs (batching, cache, quantization tradeoffs) tuned for your load profile.

Link to the pre-call folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_deliverables
